football_evidence.question: Can Indiana’s pass rush get to Minnesota’s quarterback?
football_evidence.assessment: No material disagreement: EdgeDesk and the line are within 1.8 points.
supporting: When Minnesota has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Minnesota’s offense averages 3.6 yards per carry, and Indiana’s defense allows 3.7 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).

When Minnesota has the ball (big plays on the ground): Minnesota’s offense turns 3.7% of its runs into explosive gains, and Indiana’s defense gives up explosive gains on 4.3% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Indiana has the ball (big plays on the ground): Indiana’s offense turns 8.6% of its runs into explosive gains, and Minnesota’s defense gives up explosive gains on 7.2% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).

When Minnesota has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Minnesota’s offense has allowed a sack on 1.4% of its dropbacks, and Indiana’s defense sacks the quarterback on 11.6% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
contradicting: When Indiana has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Indiana’s offense has allowed a sack on 5.4% of its dropbacks, and Minnesota’s defense sacks the quarterback on 8.9% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
In his last two games (Nebraska and Ohio State), Hoover averaged 9.0 yards per attempt, against 10.4 in his five games before that.
Minnesota comes in on 21 days of rest after an open week; Indiana has had 7 days.
quarterbacks: Josh Hoover has completed 108 of 168 passes (64.3%) for 1,661 yards, 9.9 yards per attempt, 18 touchdowns and no interceptions in seven games for Indiana, and has been sacked on 9 of 177 dropbacks.
Drake Lindsey has completed 128 of 196 passes (65.3%) for 1,350 yards, 6.9 yards per attempt, 10 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in six games for Minnesota, and has been sacked on 2 of 198 dropbacks.
